slot.brief: Two blocks connected by a light string over a smooth pulley (Atwood); write free-body equations and find acceleration and tension, then use kinematics for velocity after a given drop.

stem: Two blocks of masses $2$ kg and $3$ kg are connected by a light string over a smooth pulley and released from rest. How fast is the $3$ kg block moving after descending $2$ m? Take $g=10$ m s$^{-2}$.

verdicts.working: The acceleration is \(a=\frac{3-2}{3+2}g=2\,\text{m s}^{-2}\). From rest, \(v^2=2as=2(2)(2)=8\), so \(v=2\sqrt{2}\,\text{m s}^{-1}\).

working:
$a=\dfrac{(3-2)g}{3+2}=2$ m s$^{-2}$.\\
$3g-T=3a\Rightarrow T=24$ N.\\
$v^2=2as=2(2)(2)=8\Rightarrow v=2\sqrt{2}$ m s$^{-1}$.

Independent check: The acceleration is \(a=\frac{3-2}{3+2}g=2\,\text{m s}^{-2}\). From rest, \(v^2=2as=2(2)(2)=8\), so \(v=2\sqrt{2}\,\text{m s}^{-1}\).
solution:
For an Atwood machine, $a=\dfrac{(3-2)g}{3+2}=2\,\text{m s}^{-2}$. From rest, after descending $s=2\,\text{m}$,
$$v^2=2as=2(2)(2)=8 \quad\Rightarrow\quad v=2\sqrt{2}\,\text{m s}^{-1}.$$
